title: Per-token Impact Simulator & Price-band Composer for Cost Attribution and Export
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Teams using Redwood Console need an intuitive way to understand how minute changes in prompt composition, model selection, and batching rules change per-token unit economics and downstream invoice line-items. Current cost views are aggregated and make it hard to simulate pricing changes or produce exportable reconciliations for finance.

Goals: 1) Provide a per-token "impact simulator" that lets engineers and product owners tweak parameters (model variant, batch size, prompt prefixing, kv-cache hit assumptions, quantization profile) and immediately see marginal cost, latency delta, and projected invoice lines. 2) Offer a price-band composer UI that translates marginal figures into exportable price bands (e.g., tiered pricing, committed vs on-demand) and CSV/JSON line-items for billing systems. 3) Integrate attribution links so each exported line can trace back to conversation IDs, route IDs, and prompt families for audits and regressions.

Scope: Design includes console screens, interaction patterns for simulation, export spec, prototype flows, accessibility notes, and handoff artifacts for engineering and finance integration.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator UI enables modifying at least five parameters and shows instantaneous recalculation of per-token cost and estimated monthly spend.
Price-band composer can produce CSV and structured JSON exports that map to our internal billing ledger fields (route_id, model_variant, cost_per_token, volume_estimate, invoice_sku).
Attribution drillthrough links available for every composed line to open the Console trace + sample prompts (or report 'redacted' when required by privacy settings).
Prototype validated in user testing with at least 3 early customers and actionable feedback logged.
Design handoff includes Figma frames, interaction specs, accessibility checklist, and a prioritized engineering ticket list.
mocks: Figma frame: Simulator - baseline vs adjusted (frame 12)
Figma frame: Composer - tier bands editor (frame 18)
decisions: Use a dual-pane layout: left for parameter controls and historical sliders, right for live cost breakdown + export preview (chosen to support side-by-side mental model).

Expose only a curated set of simulation knobs initially (model_variant, avg_tokens_per_call, batch_size, kv_cache_hit_rate, quant_profile) to avoid paralysis by variables. Engineering can expand knobs behind an 'advanced' toggle.
Price bands are edited as weighted ranges rather than fixed point values to handle uncertainty — UI shows min/median/max projections and a recommended band computed from usage percentiles.
Exports will include both human-readable CSV and machine-friendly JSON with explicit provenance fields to satisfy finance and integration needs.
review_comments: 2025-02-20 - Claire Ng (PM): Asked for clearer labeling between marginal cost vs amortized cost; requires tooltip copy and short training snippet.
2025-02-26 - Sanjay Rao (Eng): Notes kernel/quantization knobs require backend sampling; suggested showing confidence intervals rather than exact numbers for certain knobs.
2025-03-01 - Lena Vogel (Finance): Approved CSV column set for reconciliation but requested 'billing_period' and 'commit_reference' be included in export schema.
2025-03-03 - Accessibility review (Yara Smith): Keyboard focus order is acceptable; color contrast needs updates on the risk-high bands.
next_steps: Incorporate review feedback into mock v2 (Aisha) — due 2025-03-07.
Create engineering spike ticket to define sampling heuristics for kv_cache_hit_rate and batch-level cost modeling (ENG-2456).
Schedule 1:1 demos with 3 pilot customers to validate exporter fields and price-band mental model (owners: Marco, Claire).
Prepare handing doc for finance integration including field mapping and sample reconciliations.
notes: Implementation hint: backend should return a small distribution sample and a deterministic median for UI to display; UI will compute percentile bands client-side for responsiveness.
Privacy: when 'redaction' is enabled tenant-level identifiers must be hashed and sample prompts truncated; include a flag in export: "redacted=true|false".
UX tradeoff: showing exact cents per token promotes trust but can be misleading — include clear 'assumptions' panel and allow users to pin an assumption set for repeated exports.
